column1: # cachegrind-baseline.tsv - instructions and D1 misses per lookup (or per request, for an evaluator
# row), D1 32 KiB of 64-byte lines, fully associative. cachegrind-gate.sh gates each within +-10% for its
# architecture and compiler. Rows are rewritten per architecture by --write-baseline.
# x86_64 clang: Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1), valgrind-3.22.0, (Ubuntu GLIBC 2.39-0ubuntu8.9) 2.39
# aarch64 clang: Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1), valgrind-3.22.0, (Ubuntu GLIBC 2.39-0ubuntu8.9) 2.39
# vantage x86_64: load 1.00 1.01 1.06 on 16 CPUs at 2026-10-19T08:52Z; control evaluator-basis-rules-4@floor timed 1174 1100 1078 ms
# vantage aarch64: load 2.61 2.52 2.99 on 8 CPUs at 2026-10-19T08:44Z; control evaluator-basis-rules-4@floor timed 813 791 791 ms
# the C library is recorded, not compared: no libc code runs between the instrumentation marks
# Since the driver measures on its own aligned stack, a D1 row is a different quantity from one
# measured on the launch stack: rows written with the launch probe in the gate are the reference,
# and an architecture's rows written before it are the old measurement until --write-baseline
# requests per run: the routing and shipped slots 1000000 per stream; lookup rows 1000000; each evaluator
# row the count the driver's slot table gives it (cg_driver <dir> slots)
